title.value: Solve a full course assignment with a coding agent

introduction.value: An instructor found Claude Code could complete an entire assignment including writeup and reflection from the assignment text alone, prompting redesigned assessments and LLM autograding.

method.value: In fall 2025, Kästner pointed Claude Code at the assignment text for a Machine Learning in Production homework: extend a small Flask Instagram clone with two AI features. It finished everything without interaction, including the writeup and reflection. He then moved the course to TA check-ins, exams and demo videos, and built LLM-as-a-judge autograding that marks work pass or needs review.

outcome.value: The old assignment became trivial, so it was replaced with a larger task in Zulip, a codebase of over 500k lines. Autograding cut TA grading time by 50 to 80%. He has no evidence on learning outcomes.

notes.value: Agent-proof designs decay as models improve, so the assignments and countermeasures need rechecking each semester. Calibrating the LLM graders' prompts also takes some tuning.

source_text.body:
Solve a full course assignment with a coding agent
An instructor found Claude Code could complete an entire assignment including writeup and reflection from the assignment text alone, prompting redesigned assessments and LLM autograding.
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
In fall 2025, Kästner pointed Claude Code at the assignment text for a Machine Learning in Production homework: extend a small Flask Instagram clone with two AI features. It finished everything without interaction, including the writeup and reflection. He then moved the course to TA check-ins, exams and demo videos, and built LLM-as-a-judge autograding that marks work pass or needs review.
How it went
The old assignment became trivial, so it was replaced with a larger task in Zulip, a codebase of over 500k lines. Autograding cut TA grading time by 50 to 80%. He has no evidence on learning outcomes.
Worth knowing
Agent-proof designs decay as models improve, so the assignments and countermeasures need rechecking each semester. Calibrating the LLM graders' prompts also takes some tuning.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Here is the assignment text for my course in [folder or file path]. Act as a student and attempt it end to end, including the writeup and reflection, then tell me which parts you finished with no extra context. Afterward, suggest [3-5] changes to the assignment or grading rubric that would make it harder for an AI to complete without real learning. Save your attempt and suggestions to a new folder and don't edit the original files.
Original source: https://thelastsoftwareengineer.substack.com/p/how-i-changed-teaching-after-ai-managed
